about: Each card's two roofline ceilings (#109), measured on this box by src/felizjueves/performance/ceilings.py's probes behind the card gate (src/felizjueves/performance/gate.py), and read by src/felizjueves/performance/device.py as Arch.fp64_flops_per_s / Arch.mem_bandwidth_bytes_per_s. A quantity with no record here is NOT CHARACTERISED (0.0): that card has no ridge and gets no verdict. Values are ACHIEVABLE rates (kind), the median over the probe's timed launches, never datasheet peaks. 'published' is the vendors' figures, a sanity bound only (a measured rate above one is a bug in the probe -- except where a card's 'per_clock' names the quantity: then the bound is flop per counted GPU cycle, the flop/s figure is at the rated clock, and a card clocking above it may exceed it, #141) and the denominator of each record's ratio_to_published; it never reaches device.py. Rewritten only by the opt-in recording run each record's 'command' names.

sm_86.source: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 (GA102) as specified by NVIDIA: 29.8 TFLOPS fp32 at the 1710 MHz rated boost, fp64 at GA102's 1:64 ratio (NVIDIA Ampere GA102 GPU Architecture whitepaper) = 0.465 TFLOPS; 10 GB GDDR6X, 320-bit at 19 Gbps = 760 GB/s.
sm_86.note: At the RATED boost clock. This card's SMI reports a 2100 MHz maximum SM clock and it ran the probe at ~1.95 GHz, so a probe reaching the hardware's issue rate could exceed 0.465 TFLOPS without a bug; the probe's best is ~0.44 (95%), so the bound has not bitten -- if a better probe trips it, check the clock before calling the probe wrong.

gfx1200.source: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (Navi 44, RDNA4): AMD publishes no fp64 figure for it. 0.4006 TFLOPS is per_clock.fp64_flops_per_s's 128 flop/clk at AMD's 3130 MHz rated boost -- derived WITHOUT AMD's 25.6 TFLOPS fp32 figure, which counts VOPD dual-issue (#141). 16 GB GDDR6, 128-bit at 20 Gbps = 320 GB/s, as specified by AMD.

fp64_flops_per_s.derivation: 32 CUs (amd-smi static --asic NUM_COMPUTE_UNITS) x 2 fp64 FMA lanes per CU per clock x 2 flop = 128 flop per GPU clock. The lane count is the 1:32 fp64 ratio third-party databases list for RDNA4 applied to the 64 fp32 FMA lanes a CU issues per clock in SINGLE issue (2 SIMD32), not to the dual-issue 128 AMD's fp32 figure counts: dual issue is VOPD, whose opcode set has no f64 operation, and the probe's gfx1200 code (hipcc --save-temps, ROCm 7.2.4) is plain v_fma_f64, 16 per loop iteration for fj_fma<16>, with no v_dual_* in the loop -- the probe is not dual-issue-shaped and cannot be.
fp64_flops_per_s.evidence: #141, measured on this box behind the gate, independent of any vendor figure: the cycle-counter pass (rocprofv3 1.1.0, GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE per fj_fma launch; ceilings.CYCLES_COMMAND) reads 127.95 flop per GPU cycle for fj_fma<16> and 127.93 for fj_fma<8> -- doubling the independent chains does not move it, so it is a throughput limit, not latency, and it sits 0.04% under 128 and at half the 256 a dual-issue fp64 rate would allow. The counted clock (cycles over the dispatch's duration) is ~3.49 GHz under fj_fma<16>, matching amd-smi's GFX_0 samples during the timed run (3.48-3.49 GHz), ABOVE both the 3130 MHz rated boost and the 2700 MHz amd-smi reports as MAX_CLK. Each recorded row's raw.per_clock carries its own counter pass.
fp64_flops_per_s.check: ceilings.check_per_clock: every counted launch's flops over its GPU cycles must be <= flop_per_clk, else ProbeBug. This bound needs no clock; the flop/s figure above is the rated-clock figure only, and the measured value may exceed it.

gfx1200.note: SETTLED (#141), the #116 assumption retired: fp64 on this card is 2 FMA lanes per CU per clock, the single-issue reading; the 0.801 TFLOPS figure that assumed dual-issue applies to fp64 is withdrawn as a bound (it was 2x too high). The measured ceiling EXCEEDS the 0.4006 TFLOPS rated-clock figure (~111%) because the card runs fp64-only work at ~3.49 GHz, above its rated boost -- the one row whose value legitimately exceeds its own flop/s figure; the bound that bites is per clock (per_clock.fp64_flops_per_s), and the probe runs at ~99.96% of it. The ridge reads the MEASURED ceiling (ceilings.gfx1200), i.e. the card at the clock it ran the probe at; it never reads this figure or the per-clock bound.
